parsed.explanation: Expanding (4) at x=x_0+nc, y=y_0+me gives (cn-em)^2 + (2c-4e)c·n + 2ce·m + const; the raw n-coefficient is 2c(c-2e), not 4c(c-e), and the m-term 2ce·m is unbounded. The displayed 4c(c-e)n is correct only after substituting em = cn + (em-cn), i.e. 2c y_m = 2c y_0 + 2c^2 n + 2c(em-cn), so the residual is 2c(em-cn)+const = O(1) precisely along |cn-em|<1 (and =const in Case 1, using cq=ep). The write-up never performs this regrouping; it asserts "+O(1)" in Case 2 while (5) only guarantees O(n+m), which cannot be dominated by a linear negative term. Decisive step asserted, not proved; one added sentence repairs it.
